intent: Bring python_pkg/wsg_grabber/catalog.py under the 250-line file cap by extracting its defensive JSON coercion helpers into a sibling module, without changing any public behaviour.
scope: Non-goal: no behaviour change, no test changes, no public API change
changes: Extracted _get/_as_list/_as_int/_as_md5 plus the _MD5_SHAPE and _INT64_MIN/_INT64_MAX constants into python_pkg/wsg_grabber/_coerce.py as module-public get/as_list/as_int/as_md5.

catalog.py now imports those four helpers from _coerce; the six public functions (media_url, parse_thread_list, parse_archive, parse_thread, deleted_md5s, new_files) keep identical signatures and behaviour.
catalog.py 251 -> 175 lines; _coerce.py is 87 lines. Both under the 250-line cap.

verification.evidence: 277 passed in 15.02s. catalog.py 61 stmts / 30 branches 100%; new _coerce.py 20 stmts / 6 branches 100%. Every wsg_grabber module at 100%, so no coverage was lost by the move and the new module is measured rather than silently skipped.
All hooks Passed, including ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit, and 'pytest with coverage enforcement'. No noqa or suppression was added.

Only importer is downloader.py, which calls the public functions parse_thread_list/parse_archive/parse_thread/new_files/deleted_md5s/media_url. No caller and no test referenced the extracted private helpers, so no re-export shim was required.

risks: A formatter stripped the new _coerce import once mid-edit (it ran while call sites still used the old _as_* names); the import was restored and re-verified by grep before the gate was run.
Low residual risk: the change is a pure move of private helpers with no signature change, covered by 277 existing tests at 100% branch coverage.
rollback: git revert the commit; catalog.py returns to its 251-line single-file form and _coerce.py is deleted.
After rollback, run python3 -m pytest python_pkg/wsg_grabber/tests/ -q to confirm 277 tests still pass.
